questions: What happens if a player chooses an index i where A_i = 0?
Is it guaranteed that the game will always end, or could it potentially run indefinitely?
What is the exact condition for winning - is it the player who makes S equal to {1,2,...,N} or the player who performs the operation when all indices have been added to S?
Can a player choose an index that has already been added to S, and if so, what happens to A_i in that case?
What is the precise definition of "playing optimally" in this context - maximizing winning probability or following a specific strategy?
Are there any restrictions on which index a player can choose, beyond the condition that A_i ≥ 1?
What happens if N = 0 - is this case excluded by the constraints or does it need special handling?
Is the input format strictly guaranteed to have exactly one line for N followed by exactly one line for the A sequence, or could there be variations in whitespace/formatting?
answers: A player may only choose i where A_i ≥ 1; choosing an index with A_i = 0 isn't a valid move.
Yes, the game is guaranteed to terminate, since S only grows and is bounded by size N.
The winning condition is performing the operation that makes S = {1,2,...,N}; that player wins.
Not explicitly restricted; choosing an index already in S is presumably allowed and simply decrements A_i without changing S.
Both players play deterministically to guarantee a win whenever one is achievable for them.
No further restriction beyond A_i ≥ 1 and 1 ≤ i ≤ N.
Not applicable; N is guaranteed to be at least 1.
Not specified beyond the given two-line format; standard whitespace-separated input is assumed.
inline_prompts: Fennec and Snuke are playing a board game. You are given a positive integer N and a sequence A=(A_1,A_2,\dots,A_N) of positive integers of length N. Also, there is a set S, which is initially empty. Fennec and Snuke take turns performing the following operation in order, starting with Fennec. - Choose an index i such that 1\leq A_i ≥ 1, subtract 1 from A_i, and if i\notin S, add i to S. - If S=\lbrace 1,2,\dots,N \rbrace, the game ends and the player who performed the last operation wins. Note that it can be proven that until a winner is determined and the game ends, players can always make a move (there exists some i such that 1\leq A_i). Both Fennec and Snuke play optimally to win. Determine who will win. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N A_1 A_2 \dots A_N Output Print Fennec if Fennec wins, or Snuke if Snuke wins. Constraints - 1\leq N\leq 2\times 10^5 - 1\leq A_i\leq 10^9 (1\leq i\leq N) - All input values are integers.
